beats.narration: Kwen three Next swaps three of every four attention layers for something whose memory never grows. What is that something, and what does it cost?

props.title: Qwen3-Next, Attention Optional?
thesis: 36 of its 48 layers swap the growing KV cache for a fixed-size memory,
updated by a gated delta rule. One layer in four keeps exact attention.

roadmap.label: The layout
roadmap.body: 12 blocks: 3 Gated DeltaNet layers + 1 gated attention.

roadmap.label: The memory
roadmap.body: A fixed state against a cache that grows with every token.

roadmap.label: The bill
roadmap.body: A fixed state compresses the past — what gets forgotten?

beats.narration: Twelve blocks of four. Three Gated DeltaNet layers, a kind of linear attention, then one gated full attention layer. Each layer routes to ten of five hundred twelve experts.
beats.narration_text: Twelve blocks of four. Three Gated DeltaNet layers, a kind of linear attention, then one gated full attention layer. Each layer routes to ten of five hundred twelve experts.

props.heading: The layout — 48 layers, 12 blocks of 4

moves.label: LINEAR
moves.detail: Layers 1–3 of each block: Gated DeltaNet, linear attention with a fixed-size state.

moves.label: FULL
moves.detail: Layer 4: full attention with an output gate — 16 query heads, 2 KV heads.

moves.label: EXPERTS
moves.detail: After every layer: 10 of 512 routed experts, plus 1 shared.

moves.label: SCALE
moves.detail: 80B parameters in total, 3B active per token; 262,144-token context.

props.keepNote: Row 1 is the bet: three layers in four never grow their memory.

beats.narration: Each DeltaNet head keeps one fixed matrix. Per token, a gate fades the old memory, then the delta rule corrects what it got wrong. It never grows.
beats.narration_text: Each DeltaNet head keeps one fixed matrix. Per token, a gate fades the old memory, then the delta rule corrects what it got wrong. It never grows.

props.heading: Gated DeltaNet — one token, one update

moves.label: STATE
moves.detail: One 128 × 128 matrix S per value head; 32 value heads per layer.

moves.label: GATE
moves.detail: Fade the old memory a little: S ← α·S, with α between 0 and 1.

moves.label: DELTA
moves.detail: Correct the guess: add β·(v − S·k), the error on this token's value, along its key k.

moves.label: READ
moves.detail: Output o = S·q. S is the same size at token 10 or token 262,144.

props.keepNote: Row 3 is the idea: fix what the memory gets wrong, instead of appending every token.
props.source: Yang, Kautz & Hatamizadeh — Gated Delta Networks, arXiv:2412.06464 §3.1 eq. 10 · Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct config.json

beats.narration: A full attention layer caches a thousand twenty-four numbers per token. A DeltaNet layer: half a million, at any length. Break-even at five hundred twelve tokens. At full context, five hundred twelve times smaller.
beats.narration_text: A full attention layer caches a thousand twenty-four numbers per token. A DeltaNet layer: half a million, at any length. Break-even at five hundred twelve tokens. At full context, five hundred twelve times smaller.

props.heading: Memory per layer — millions of values
props.exception: Break-even is 512 tokens — both hold 524,288 values. The 512x gap needs the full 262,144.
props.source: Computed from config.json: 2 KV heads × 256 × (K,V) = 1,024 values/token · state 32 × 128 × 128

beats.narration: Verdict: attention isn't optional, it's rationed. One layer in four keeps exact lookup; the rest compress. The savings are real. The question is what gets forgotten.

artifactLines: Layout: 36 Gated DeltaNet + 12 gated full-attention layers (3:1).
Memory: a DeltaNet layer's state is fixed — equal to a full layer's cache at 512 tokens, 512x smaller at 262K.
Cost: a fixed state compresses the past, so exact recall isn't guaranteed — 1 layer in 4 keeps it.
